Barbell_Full_Squat: Set the bar in the rack at upper-chest height. Step under it and rest it on your upper back, not on your neck.
Grip it slightly wider than your shoulders, unrack the bar and take two steps back. Feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly.
Breathe in, brace your abs and lower by pushing your hips back and down, knees tracking over your toes.
Go as low as you can keep your back neutral (ideally with your thighs at least parallel to the floor) and stand up by pushing the floor away with your whole foot.
Tip: do not let your knees cave in or your heels lift. Use the rack's safety bars.
Front_Barbell_Squat: Rest the bar on the front of your shoulders, close to your neck, with your elbows high and pointing forward.
Hold it with your fingers (clean grip) or with your arms crossed over it; what matters is that it rests on your shoulders, not your wrists.
With your feet shoulder-width apart, lower with your torso as upright as possible and your elbows up.
Stand up by pushing through your whole foot without letting your elbows drop or your chest tip forward.
Dumbbell_Squat: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and your feet shoulder-width apart.
Lower by pushing your hips back and down, chest up and knees following your feet.
Go down until your thighs are parallel to the floor or as far as you can keep your back straight.
Stand up by pushing the floor away with your whole foot until your legs are straight.
Goblet_Squat: Hold a kettlebell or dumbbell with both hands in front of your chest, elbows pointing down.
Set your feet slightly wider than your shoulders, toes turned out a little.
Sink down between your legs, keeping your chest up and the weight close to your body; your elbows can brush the inside of your knees.
Stand up by pushing through your whole foot. It is a great variation to learn to squat with a straight back.
Squats_-_With_Bands: Stand on the band with both feet, shoulder-width apart, and pass the other end behind your neck or hold it at shoulder height.
Lower by pushing your hips back, chest up and knees in line with your feet.
Stand up by pushing the floor away: the band resists more as your legs straighten, so finish the movement with control.
Bodyweight_Squat: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms out in front or crossed over your chest.
Lower by pushing your hips back and down as if sitting on a chair, with your heels down.
Go down until your thighs are parallel to the floor or as far as you can keep your back straight.
Stand up by pushing through your whole foot.
Split_Squats: Take a long step forward so that both feet point ahead; your back heel is lifted.
Lower straight down by bending both knees until the back one almost touches the floor.
Stand up by pushing through the front leg. Do all the reps and switch sides.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee in line with your foot.
Barbell_Deadlift: Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet, feet hip-width apart.
Bend your hips and knees and grab the bar just outside your legs. Back straight, chest up and shoulders over the bar.
Breathe in, brace your abs and stand up by pushing the floor away with your legs, keeping the bar against your legs throughout.
Finish standing tall by extending your hips, without leaning back. Lower along the same path, pushing your hips back first.
Tip: if your back rounds, reduce the weight. Less load with good technique is better.
Romanian_Deadlift: Stand with the bar in your hands at thigh height and your feet hip-width apart.
With your knees slightly bent and fixed, push your hips back and lower the bar close to your legs.
Go down until you feel a stretch in the back of your thighs, usually just below the knees, without rounding your back.
Come up by driving your hips forward and squeezing your glutes.
Stiff-Legged_Dumbbell_Deadlift: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs and your knees almost straight.
Hinge forward by pushing your hips back and let the dumbbells travel down close to your legs, with a straight back.
Go down until you feel the stretch in your hamstrings and come back up squeezing your glutes.
Do not fully lock your knees or round your back to go lower.
One-Arm_Kettlebell_Swings: Place the kettlebell slightly in front of your feet, which are a little wider than your hips. Grab it with one hand.
Hike it back between your legs by hinging at the hips, with a straight back.
Extend your hips explosively so the kettlebell rises to chest height; your arm only guides it.
Let it fall and go into the next rep by pushing your hips back. Switch hands each set.
It is a hip movement, not a squat or a shoulder raise.
Band_Good_Morning: Stand on the band with both feet and pass the other end behind your neck, over your shoulders.
With your knees slightly bent, lean your torso forward, pushing your hips back with a straight back.
Go down until your torso is almost parallel to the floor or you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Come back up by extending your hips and squeezing your glutes.
Barbell_Hip_Thrust: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and the bar over your hips (use a pad).
Plant your feet hip-width apart with your knees bent.
Raise your hips by driving through your heels until your torso is in line with your thighs. Squeeze your glutes for a second.
Lower with control. Keep your chin tucked so you do not arch your lower back.
Single_Leg_Glute_Bridge: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat. Extend one leg up or out in front.
Push through the heel of the planted leg and raise your hips until your knee, hips and shoulders are aligned.
Squeeze the glute for a second at the top and lower with control. Do all the reps and switch sides.
Leg_Press: Sit in the leg press with your back and hips firmly against the pad and your feet on the platform shoulder-width apart.
Release the safeties and lower the platform by bending your knees towards your chest, without your hips lifting off the seat.
Push through your whole foot until your legs are almost straight, without locking your knees.
Put the safeties back on when you finish.
Barbell_Walking_Lunge: With the bar on your upper back, as for a squat, take a long step forward.
Lower until your back knee almost touches the floor, with your torso upright.
Push through the front leg and bring the back leg straight into the next step.
You need clear space around you. If you lose your balance, try the dumbbell version first.
Dumbbell_Lunges: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Take a long step forward and lower until both knees are at about 90 degrees.
Push through the front leg to return to the start and alternate legs.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee in line with your foot.
Lunge_Pass_Through: Stand with a kettlebell in one hand.
Step back and lower into a lunge. At the bottom, pass the kettlebell under your front leg to the other hand.
Return to the start and repeat with the other leg, passing the kettlebell under again.
Keep your torso upright and your abs braced throughout.
Dumbbell_Step_Ups: Stand facing a stable bench or box with a dumbbell in each hand.
Place one whole foot on the bench and step up by pushing through that leg, without pushing off with the bottom one.
At the top, straighten the leg and step down with control, lowering the last foot up first.
Do all the reps on one leg or alternate. Choose a height at which your knee does not rise above your hip.
Bodyweight_Walking_Lunge: Stand with your hands on your waist or free.
Take a long step forward and lower until your back knee almost touches the floor.
Push through the front leg and bring the back leg straight into the next step.
Keep moving forward with your torso upright.
Barbell_Lunge: Stand with the bar on your upper back and your feet hip-width apart.
Take a long step forward and lower until your back knee almost touches the floor.
Push through the front leg to return to the start and alternate legs.
Use a weight with which you can control your balance well.
Split_Squat_with_Dumbbells: Rest the top of your back foot on a bench and step the other foot forward; hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Lower straight down by bending your front knee until your thigh is almost parallel to the floor.
Stand up by pushing through the front leg. Do all the reps and switch sides.
Find a distance from the bench at which your front knee does not travel far past your toes.
Lying_Leg_Curls: Lie face down on the machine with the pad just above your heels and your knees slightly past the edge of the bench.
Hold the handles and bend your knees, bringing your heels towards your glutes.
Squeeze for a second at the top and lower with control, without lifting your hips off the bench.
Seated_Leg_Curl: Sit in the machine with your back supported and set the pad just above your heels.
Lower the thigh pad so your thighs cannot lift.
Bend your knees, taking your heels down and back, hold for a second and return with control.
Ball_Leg_Curl: Lie on your back with your heels on an exercise ball and your arms on the floor.
Raise your hips until your body is in line from shoulders to feet.
Without dropping your hips, bend your knees, rolling the ball towards your glutes.
Straighten your legs again with control.
Floor_Glute-Ham_Raise: Kneel on a soft surface and have someone hold your ankles or hook them under something solid.
With your body straight from knees to head, lower yourself forward as slowly as you can.
Catch yourself with your hands at the bottom and use them to help you back up.
It is very demanding: start with few reps and short ranges.
Leg_Extensions: Sit in the machine with your back supported and the pad on the lower part of your shins.
Straighten your legs fully without lifting your hips off the seat.
Hold for a second and lower with control.
Single-Leg_Leg_Extension: Sit in the leg extension machine with the pad on the lower part of one shin.
Straighten that leg fully, hold for a second and lower with control.
Do all the reps and switch legs. It helps even out strength differences between legs.
Weighted_Sissy_Squat: Stand holding a plate against your chest, holding a stable support with the other hand if you need it.
Rise onto your toes and push your knees forward while leaning your body back, in a straight line from knees to head.
Go as low as you can with control and come back up by squeezing your quads.
It loads the knee heavily: start without weight and with a small range.
Standing_Calf_Raises: Stand in the machine with your shoulders under the pads and the balls of your feet on the edge of the step.
Lower your heels as far as you can to stretch your calves.
Rise onto your toes as high as possible, hold for a second and lower with control.
Keep your knees straight but not locked.
Standing_Barbell_Calf_Raise: Stand with the bar on your upper back and your feet hip-width apart. You can put the balls of your feet on a plate.
Rise onto your toes as high as possible and hold for a second.
Lower with control. Do it inside the rack for safety.
Standing_Dumbbell_Calf_Raise: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand and the balls of your feet on a step.
Lower your heels to stretch and rise onto your toes as high as possible.
Hold for a second at the top and lower with control.
Seated_Calf_Raise: Sit in the machine with the balls of your feet on the platform and the pad on your thighs, near your knees.
Lower your heels to stretch and rise onto your toes as high as possible.
Hold for a second and lower with control. It mainly works the soleus.
Calf_Raises_-_With_Bands: Stand on the band with the balls of your feet and hold the ends at shoulder height.
Rise onto your toes as high as possible, hold for a second and lower with control.
